title: Book reading routes: 24-persona editorial simulation
scope: All eight chapter openings plus selected worked examples, boundaries and models listed in evidence. Not an exhaustive line-by-line review of all 726 pages.
provenance: One analyst applying the canonical 24 profiles. Native subagent dispatch was blocked by the isolation guard; no independent agent reviews or human interviews occurred.
methodology: Scores are ordinal editorial predictions, not measured behavior. Interviews are follow-up thought experiments in paraphrase. No old score was converted; no causal pre/post gain is asserted.

friction.scale: 1 low friction to 5 blocking for the persona's intended reading task

appeal.scale: 1 weak to 10 strong support for that reader's next reading decision
appeal.calculation: I/U/T each mean of three values. Individual total sums nine values, out of 90. Do not aggregate into a Book score or population estimate.

E0.label: Entry routes and evidence/status vocabulary
E0.scope: Front matter, how-to-use text, five-lane reading map and four course orders

E1.label: Local writer, authority and deployment boundary
E1.scope: Opening stack, reference-monitor discussion, maturity distinctions and conclusion

E2.label: Durability by fault class
E2.scope: NORMAL/FULL table, process crash versus OS/power loss, recovery example

E3.label: Delegated permission and its limits
E3.scope: PID example, phase overview, attenuation and qualified verification conclusion

E4.label: Confined release and channel assumptions
E4.scope: Opening work order, Derek/Erin gates, zero/one/two-bit release example and empirical taint assumption

E5.label: Mara's six-agent afternoon
E5.scope: Worked failure scenario; not evidence of a deployed interface

E6.label: Scoped, expiring consent
E6.scope: Grant tuple, stakes/reversibility conditions, example and revocation

E7.label: Summary and inspectable evidence
E7.scope: Scott analogy and two summary rows with equal compression but different artifact access

E8.label: Local identity versus cross-operator attestation
E8.scope: Two definitions, partial local implementation and unresolved cross-operator binding

E9.label: A complete three-sided settlement
E9.scope: Bob, Alice, Dana and Carol; 460 escrow, 100 bond, conditional transfers and refunds

E10.label: Advisory ClaimFile in the formal model
E10.scope: English action overview and TLA+ state/actions

E11.label: Federated revocation under delay/partition
E11.scope: Reliable-round expectation, partition boundary, attack window and rollback negative control

E12.label: Taxonomy's conflicting file-claim description
E12.scope: Advisory file/region announcement described as preventing double claims by uniqueness

E13.label: Complete illustrated contents
E13.scope: Actual full-book contents pages with all eight chapter plates and part plates

personas.name: Priya Desai
personas.route: Practitioner lane suggests a long detour for a reader who only wants her three local projects to stop colliding. Enter at the local-writer example and the resource boundary; skip the markets.
personas.observation: The port-conflict problem is immediately recognizable. The boundary between recording a reservation and controlling the process that actually listens is less easy to extract.
objections: A book must not become a prerequisite for ordinary use.
An advisory file claim is not an exclusive port reservation.
She cannot tell from the route where she has learned enough.

follow_up.question: What would make this a useful five-minute read even if you never installed anything?
follow_up.synthetic_response: She would leave once she could explain which collision is prevented, what remains outside the daemon, and where to find separate operational instructions.

personas.recommendation: Add a one-example local coordination route with an explicit exit to current documentation; do not direct her to the economics chapters.

personas.name: Marcus Webb
personas.route: Start with the same-machine boundary, then one permission example. The systems-engineer lane is too broad for deciding whether four unrelated client repositories need changes.
personas.observation: The PID example makes inherited authority concrete, but it does not answer whether adopting conventions changes a client's existing setup.
objections: Examples assume a coherent work environment he does not own.
He needs compatibility boundaries, not another repository convention.
A copied terminal excerpt can be mistaken for a supported integration recipe.

follow_up.question: What is the first detail you would check before bringing this near a client's repository?
follow_up.synthetic_response: Whether the example requires changing the client's files, scripts, credentials, or process ownership; the Book does not establish that integration result.

personas.recommendation: State what the research example assumes about the host; link to a separate compatibility guide only when that guide and its claims are verified.

personas.name: Yuki Tanaka
personas.route: Use the systems/security lanes, but jump directly from the local writer to attenuation and the file-claim model. Read the implementation boundary before treating an example as a guarantee.
personas.observation: Concrete definitions and a source path are persuasive. Conflicting uses of 'claim' would make him discount more polished claims elsewhere.
objections: A test or model name is not revision-bound evidence.
File claims switch between advisory and exclusive semantics.
A model-to-runtime gap cannot be repaired by confident summary prose.

follow_up.question: Which discrepancy would you investigate before any other?
follow_up.synthetic_response: He would reconcile the taxonomy's impossible-double-claim statement with ClaimFile's always-successful behavior, then inspect the actual enforcement point.

personas.recommendation: Add a typed-resource crosswalk and a revision-bound evidence pointer beside each model-to-implementation claim.

personas.name: Jordan Ellis
personas.route: Enter at Mara's afternoon, continue to consent and the implementation boundary, then stop. The practitioner lane should not require personhood or federation theory before that decision.
personas.observation: The falsely green report and constrained approval resemble demo-day problems. The reader still has to distinguish a proposed oversight mechanism from an available small-team workflow.
objections: No dedicated operator can be assumed.
Illustrated consent does not prove it exists in the current product.
The reading route has no small-team stopping decision.

follow_up.question: What would you take back to your team tomorrow?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A rule for checking evidence before approving consequential work, not a promise that the proposed interface or enforcement path is already available.

personas.recommendation: Put implementation status beside the consent example and end the short route with a decision the team can make without adopting new software.

personas.name: Sam Okafor
personas.route: Read local authority and the practitioner example. Consult federation only to understand what a collection of independent local installations does not provide.
personas.observation: The local coordination model could clarify team conventions. The reading map blurs sharing conventions across laptops with sharing authority across operators.
objections: Twelve independent laptops are not automatically a federated harbor.
Nothing reviewed demonstrates cross-machine setup parity.
A theory chapter does not supply rollout acceptance criteria.

follow_up.question: What evidence would let three volunteers become a team-wide pilot?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A documented environment matrix and a recovery record for a mismatch; those are external deployment evidence, not outcomes inferred from this Book.

personas.recommendation: Add a brief local-installations versus cross-operator-authority distinction. Keep pilot procedures outside the research argument.

personas.name: Devon Cole
personas.route: Read Mara, compare the two summary rows, then check the status boundary before using the material in a team presentation.
personas.observation: The summary-to-artifact comparison is an effective explanation. Its vividness risks being mistaken for a demonstration of shipped behavior.
objections: He needs a presentable case with one clear result.
A designed screen is not a recording of a working system.
The same explanation must survive Sam's implementation questions.

follow_up.question: What would make you comfortable showing this to Sam?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A clearly labeled illustrated case, an explicit list of proposed parts, and a link to the evidence for anything described as running.

personas.recommendation: Package one explanatory spread as a concept demonstration, with no live-demo claim until an actual recording and reset procedure exist.

personas.name: Rachel Kim
personas.route: Follow the security lane through the local enforcement boundary, attenuation and release-channel assumptions, then federated revocation. Skip operator psychology on the first pass.
personas.observation: Explicit hostile-operator and partition exclusions are valuable. Terminology drift around claims weakens confidence that the threat models stay separate.
objections: A shared database does not establish compulsory file mediation.
Confinement depends on the named channel assumptions.
Expected gossip time is not a hard deadline during partition.

follow_up.question: Which sentence would you refuse to approve without a narrower scope?
follow_up.synthetic_response: Any statement that implies an advisory claim prevents an actual conflicting edit, or that cross-operator revocation has a finite deadline without network assumptions.

personas.recommendation: Put each guarantee, excluded adversary and evidence class together; resolve the claim/lock vocabulary before broad visual polishing.

personas.name: Tomás Herrera
personas.route: Start at local authority and consent, then read identity and federation boundaries. The map's systems-engineer row gives no team-scale governance stopping point.
personas.observation: He can see a useful decomposition of authority. The Book is less direct about how that decomposition constrains forty teams with different owners.
objections: A relay is not a shared policy authority.
Different teams cannot be treated as one trusted operator.
An architectural principle is not a rollout ownership model.

follow_up.question: What is the smallest decision this reading should let you make?
follow_up.synthetic_response: Identify which organization owns each enforcement point and where evidence crosses an authority boundary, without claiming a deployment design has been validated.

personas.recommendation: Add an ownership-boundary example with two teams and one refused request; keep operational scaling claims conditional.

personas.name: Angela Brooks
personas.route: Take the crash route first, then recovery and revocation under delay. Stop when she can name the failure classes and unresolved recovery obligations.
personas.observation: The NORMAL/FULL table gives a useful comparison; the partition qualification prevents a misleading availability promise.
objections: Durability, integrity and successful recovery are different outcomes.
A negative control in a model is not a tested operational runbook.
Actual recovery timing and observability remain unmeasured here.

follow_up.question: What would you want next to the crash table?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A small before/crash/restart record naming what persisted, what was checked, what refused service, and what remains unknown.

personas.recommendation: Attach a reproducible failure trace to one recovery case, with the tested runtime/version and explicit limits.

personas.name: David Chen
personas.route: Use the coordination scenario for the problem and the settlement example for the institutional proposal. Leave before treating either as an investment case.
personas.observation: The failure costs are plausible and understandable. No inspected passage establishes measured return, adoption cost, support exposure or vendor continuity.
objections: A mathematically balanced settlement is not an ROI study.
He needs operating cost and support/exit information.
The reading lane does not distinguish strategic explanation from buying evidence.

follow_up.question: What can this book responsibly change in a budget conversation?
follow_up.synthetic_response: It can improve the questions for a measured pilot; it cannot establish a payback period from synthetic examples.

personas.recommendation: Give decision-makers a short concept-and-limit route and a separate list of evidence a pilot would have to collect.

personas.name: Fatima Al-Sayed
personas.route: Read release-channel assumptions, consent and identity scope. Stop at an incomplete-evidence determination rather than attempting the full security lane.
personas.observation: Explicit consent and evidence boundaries are useful concepts, but they do not supply a current data inventory or control record.
objections: Theoretical confinement is not a completed security intake.
Local identity cannot stand in for cross-organization identity binding.
Who retains, accesses and deletes data must be shown for the actual system.

follow_up.question: What would keep you from rejecting this as irrelevant while still withholding approval?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A clear statement of the threat model and a list of the current artifacts still required for intake, with no compliance claim attached to the theory.

personas.recommendation: Label the Book as explanatory research and point to a separately maintained operational evidence packet when one exists.

personas.name: Grace Liu
personas.route: Use the local writer, a crash counterexample and the attenuation verification boundary as a technical interview route, not the complete systems lane.
personas.observation: Concrete tradeoffs offer stronger interview material than self-assessed novelty. Authorship and delivery attribution still need independent verification.
objections: A polished manuscript does not prove authorship of every implementation.
Formal and runtime work must be distinguished.
She wants choices and tradeoffs, not repeated claims of rigor.

follow_up.question: What would you ask the author to explain without the manuscript?
follow_up.synthetic_response: Why one writer helps, which crash claim it does not establish, and where the verified model stops matching runtime behavior.

personas.recommendation: Add a compact artifact-and-authorship index for the reviewed mechanisms; preserve the counterexamples and unresolved obligations.

personas.name: Ben Sorensen
personas.route: Read one architecture problem, one explicit implementation boundary and the conclusion. The Book is supporting material for a delivery discussion, not delivery proof.
personas.observation: The clear limits help establish judgment. Repeated architectural ambition makes it harder to find a completed, attributed outcome.
objections: Research scope is not a completed client engagement.
He needs the boundary of the author's contribution.
The Book cannot replace a dated delivery case.

follow_up.question: What would make this useful before a contract discussion?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A short, separately evidenced case that identifies the starting problem, the author's contribution, the delivered result and the parts still open.

personas.recommendation: Provide a genuine delivery case outside the Book; do not manufacture a success anecdote to improve appeal.

personas.name: Priyanka Rao
personas.route: Read the title, plain-language claim and one illustrated chapter entry. The five technical role lanes do not provide a recruiting-summary route.
personas.observation: The chapter plates make the publication easier to recognize, but vocabulary about institutions and enforcement can obscure the author's concrete technical area.
objections: Two minutes is not enough to learn the Book's ontology.
A memorable description must not overstate delivered work.
She needs a one-sentence account she can repeat accurately.

follow_up.question: What sentence could you forward without translating the terminology?
follow_up.synthetic_response: The book studies how multiple software agents share resources, record their work and remain accountable, while separating working mechanisms from research proposals.

personas.recommendation: Keep that plain-language description near the opening and link to one representative chapter; let her stop there.

personas.name: Jake Malone
personas.route: Enter at Mara's afternoon and the two summaries. None of the five named roles obviously fits a curious friend with no reason to study the complete machinery.
personas.observation: The deleted test and falsely green report can be retold without mathematical training. The Hobbes/Scott vocabulary introduces an avoidable second translation task.
objections: He needs an ordinary reason to care before the abstractions.
Unexplained nouns can make confusion feel like a personal failure.
He should not have to pretend to be a systems engineer.

follow_up.question: What part would you retell to someone else?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A reassuring summary can conceal a bad change; the useful summary lets someone inspect what actually happened.

personas.recommendation: Offer a clearly optional story-first route with a stop after that distinction; avoid an extra glossary detour.

personas.name: Dr. Elena Vasquez
personas.route: Use the security route selectively: one authority example, the confined-release model and its assumptions. Do not presume familiarity with coding-tool acronyms.
personas.observation: Named assumptions and a worked bit-budget example provide an intellectually serious entry. The terminology makes disciplinary transfer harder than the mathematics itself.
objections: Which results are mathematical and which are empirical must remain visible.
A metaphor is not evidence for a behavioral generalization.
The finite model's excluded channels need plain-language explanation.

follow_up.question: Where would an example help more than another definition?
follow_up.synthetic_response: Immediately before the formal release model: show what can leave, what cannot, and one excluded channel that defeats the guarantee.

personas.recommendation: Keep the proof route intact and add a prerequisite/notation bridge for technically sophisticated readers outside software security.

personas.name: Theo Marsh
personas.route: Start with Mara, consent and evidence-backed summaries, then inspect lifecycle semantics. He should not need the institutional-theory lane to judge the oversight idea.
personas.observation: The problem matches daily multi-agent work. The clearest missing distinction is what the interface proposes versus what an enforcement path actually rejects.
objections: A useful oversight concept does not prove increased agent capacity.
Advisory coordination must not masquerade as mandatory exclusion.
He needs a task-level result with human review cost included.

follow_up.question: What would make the next example convincing rather than merely familiar?
follow_up.synthetic_response: The same task under stated conditions, including failed attempts, review effort and what the system refused; synthetic quantities must remain labeled.

personas.recommendation: Design a bounded comparison protocol for later measurement; do not add an unsupported productivity percentage.

personas.name: Nadia Petrov
personas.route: Select the summary comparison as a visual explanation and check the status boundary. The illustrated contents help locate material but are not themselves a demo sequence.
personas.observation: The contrast between an assertion and inspectable evidence is visually teachable. Long captions and undefined side notes dilute a short explanation.
objections: One screen should make one change in understanding.
She needs to know which visual is hypothetical.
A live-demo promise requires reproducible behavior, not nicer artwork.

follow_up.question: Which ninety-second story is worth making?
follow_up.synthetic_response: One green report, the underlying bad diff, and the evidence view that exposes the difference, explicitly labeled as an illustrated case unless recorded from a working system.

personas.recommendation: Create a short explainer from a verified case; pair any eventual live recording with provenance and a reset procedure.

personas.name: Chris Whitfield
personas.route: Use a crash example, attenuation and one settlement as separate lessons. The four proposed course orders need prerequisites and assessable endpoints, not just chapter sequences.
personas.observation: The small counterexamples and arithmetic can teach transferable patterns. Branded terminology can obscure what transfers beyond this project.
objections: A chapter list is not a teaching plan.
Learners need to know the prerequisite for each jump.
One lesson should end in an answer they can check.

follow_up.question: What would make one of these examples teachable next week?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A short prerequisite statement, one worked case, one altered assumption and an answer or counterexample, without requiring the full Book.

personas.recommendation: Add a lesson-sized route for one existing check/trace exercise; do not claim the courses have been classroom-tested.

personas.name: Morgan Reyes
personas.route: Read one collision or Mara's example first. The practitioner lane presupposes enough vocabulary that a new developer may not recognize it as the beginner route.
personas.observation: Named people and concrete events help. WAL, capability attenuation and identity vocabulary accumulate before the reader has a stable mental picture.
objections: The first useful result is too far from the unfamiliar terms.
She needs an explanation of why a losing request is refused.
A long proof should be optional on the first encounter.

follow_up.question: At what point would you know you had understood the example?
follow_up.synthetic_response: When she can predict which request succeeds, what evidence records the result, and one action the system cannot prevent.

personas.recommendation: Add a no-install trace with three visible steps and a checkable answer before the formal vocabulary.

personas.name: Aisha Bello
personas.route: Take the coordination entry route and the identity boundary. Neither mechanism designer nor institutional theorist precisely names her stakeholder-briefing task.
personas.observation: The consent example supports a useful discussion of who approves consequential work. It is easy to miss that design intent and available capability are different.
objections: She needs consequences and ownership, not command syntax.
A future mechanism must not enter a roadmap as a present feature.
A brief needs a stopping conclusion.

follow_up.question: What should a stakeholder understand after your summary?
follow_up.synthetic_response: Who may authorize the action, what evidence they can inspect, and which enforcement or identity assumptions remain unresolved.

personas.recommendation: Provide a short stakeholder route ending with those three questions and a current-status pointer.

personas.name: Liam O'Connor
personas.route: Read the fault-class example, then a check/trace exercise; use the settlement arithmetic or formal model as an optional second lesson.
personas.observation: Worked arithmetic and a counterexample offer a concrete learning payoff. A dense route map can conceal that a small exercise is enough for a first sitting.
objections: He needs prerequisite hints before changing disciplines.
Model syntax can arrive before an English state picture.
A solution link should support checking, not replace the attempt.

follow_up.question: What would make you come back for a second sitting?
follow_up.synthetic_response: Successfully predict one failure or settle one small transaction, then see which changed assumption produces a different answer.

personas.recommendation: Promote one existing check/trace/solution loop as an optional first exercise and give a clear resume point.

personas.name: Sophie Turner
personas.route: Read the opening plain-language claim and one worked incident. The five professional reading lanes offer no honest nontechnical exit.
personas.observation: The book can explain why evidence matters, but most of its technical depth is unrelated to her immediate reason for opening it.
objections: She cannot distinguish harmless jargon from a prerequisite.
A full reading assignment would be inappropriate.
A polished artifact alone does not establish the author's practical claims.

follow_up.question: What would count as enough, without turning you into a specialist?
follow_up.synthetic_response: Be able to ask what changed, what checked it and who is responsible, then leave with a more informed question for a developer.

personas.recommendation: Provide a one-scene general-interest route. Treat her decision not to continue as a valid outcome.

personas.name: Victor Aldana
personas.route: Challenge the attractive routes after the other profiles: compare the file-claim statements, inspect the local/cross-operator split and remove the revocation network assumption.
personas.observation: Explicit negative controls and unresolved boundaries are the strongest material. Rhetorical certainty or a clean diagram cannot compensate for mismatched scopes.
objections: Terminology contradicts the later model.
Named scripts do not establish current successful execution.
A compelling scenario is not evidence that its mechanism is deployed.

follow_up.question: What would change your view without asking you to trust the author?
follow_up.synthetic_response: A reconciled scope statement, a reproducible revision-bound witness and a deliberately failing case when a required assumption is removed.

personas.recommendation: Resolve contradictions before claiming broad usability gains; keep the failure case adjacent to the positive result.
